claims.text: Significant atomic-size mismatches increase local lattice distortion in high-entropy alloys.
Increased lattice distortion impedes dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion increases yield strength.
Atomic-size differences generate internal stress fields through severe local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions hinder dislocation glide.
Local lattice distortions promote dislocation pinning.
X-ray diffraction peak broadening can be used to quantify the extent of local lattice distortion.
Alloys with greater measured lattice distortion are expected to have greater hardness than low-distortion baseline alloys.
Alloys with greater measured lattice distortion are expected to have greater yield strength than low-distortion baseline alloys.
The proposed relationship applies to single-phase, solid-solution high-entropy alloys with predominantly FCC or BCC structures under ambient conditions.
The proposed relationship may not govern hardness and strength when precipitation, twinning, or phase transformations dominate strengthening.
The magnitude of the lattice-distortion effect may vary with microstructural factors and measurement uncertainty.

Failure to observe a positive relationship between measured lattice distortion and both hardness and yield strength would falsify lattice distortion as the dominant controlling factor under the stated conditions.
